description: DENSE: five defects across four areas, with TWO on logistics and two SKUs that must be judged separately. Every mandatory document is present so the completeness gate passes and the reviewers actually run - an earlier draft omitted the electrical safety certificate, which made the gate short-circuit and rebuilt the exact F03 trap inside a fixture meant to test the opposite thing. The certificate is now present but its scope covers only one of the two SKUs.

expected.note: The certificate is present, in date, and names a real standard - so a completeness check passes and a date check passes. It covers 'LED floodlights, 30W to 150W' only, and RAV-BAT-04 is a 40W batten luminaire, which is outside that range. Present-but-out-of-scope is the case a reviewer that checks existence and expiry will clear. NOT modelled as a missing document on purpose: that would make the gate short-circuit and the other four defects unreachable, which is the F03 trap this fixture exists to avoid.
Product liability GBP 3m against a GBP 5m minimum. Public liability is GBP 10m and passes, so reading only the first line clears this vendor.

28.4kg against a 25kg manual handling limit, direct to store where there is no forklift. Comfortably over rather than marginal, so this should read as MAJOR - the contrast with F18's deliberately marginal 26.0kg.

The GS1 certificate gives the company prefix as 5033333 and RAV-BAT-04's GTIN starts 6011111 - a barcode belonging to someone else, most likely the original manufacturer. The other SKU's GTIN matches correctly, so this cannot be found by checking one SKU and generalising.
One open overdue major beside one closed minor. Counting non-conformances gives two; what matters is that one is open, major and past its due date.
